name: Derro
body:
A derro (sometimes spelled dero) is a small, dwarf-like humanoid native to the deepest subterranean realms. Corrupted by an unknown magical affliction, derros are cursed by a madness that twists their minds and warps their perception of reality, turning them cruel and spiteful. Most derros become paranoid and jealous, believing that all non-derros are thieves who have stolen what rightfully belongs to them—whether that is knowledge, treasure, or the secrets of life under the bright sun of the surface world.

Physical

Derros are short in stature with lumpy bodies and spindly limbs. They are often described as having features that resemble twisted gnomes or tortured dwarves, and are sometimes mistaken for these peoples—although the differences seem obvious to anyone familiar with the species.

A derro’s skin is pale white, gray, or blue, but may feature patches of pink, purple, green, or tan. Their pure white hair is always wild and unkempt, even among the most disciplined derros. The men often grow long mustaches, and a few also grow short beards.

Derros have only four digits on each hand and foot. Their ears are pointed and their bulging eyes are solid white. They are prone to wearing a variety of specialized fabrics and leathers, all of which seem to be adorned with an overabundance of sashes, cinches, straps, snaps, clasps, belts, buckles, pouches, pockets, and all manner of strange contraptions.

Social

Most derros are obsessed with the surface world, believing it holds treasures meant for them that they can never obtain because of their weakness to sunlight. They often form raiding parties to kidnap surface-dwellers, whom they then conduct horrible experiments upon, determined to learn the secret of surviving in the sunlight. While these experiments have been known to sometimes accidentally yield success for an individual derro or two, a cure for the species as a whole has eluded them.

Ultimately, the derros’ intrinsic madness seems to doom them to perpetual frustration in this quest.

Derro communities are only loosely organized. They tend to follow the lead of the strongest among them, giving the most deference to those with the greatest mastery over the arcane. Derro communities are held together by their shared goals, as well as their deep distrust of others, but they remain a jumble of mad schemes and conflicting ideas.

Occasionally a lone derro will strike out independently from their community—determined to assess their prospects without any interference from other derros.

These adventuring types are usually the most miserable and conflicted of all.

Alignment And Religion

Driven to paranoia and madness by their affliction, derros naturally gravitate to the Chaotic alignments, and most are also Evil.

Although they may try to make other plans, their minds inevitably come back to sadistic thoughts of conquest and destruction.

Not all derros concern themselves with religion, but many derro communities encourage demon worship for those who do practice some kind of faith.

Names

Some typical derro names include the following (choose or roll 1d12): 1 Badbertax, 2 Bitimanax, 3 Bizeraki, 4 Gogoax, 5 Koruluzaz, 6 Koskalixa, 7 Makunziok, 8 Obsejelotaz, 9 Spirenzek, 10 Urdinix, 11 Uzopuluak, 12 Zumurrutik

Standard Species Traits
Ability Score Modifiers You are hearty, quick, and maddeningly charismatic, but physically slight and mentally afflicted. Your ability score modifiers are +2 Dex, +2 Con, +2 Cha, –2 Str, –4 Wis [mixed weakness, advanced Dex]. (2)
Size As a Small creature, you have a +1 size bonus on attack rolls, a +1 size bonus to your Armor Class, a –1 size penalty to your CMB, and a +4 size bonus on Stealth checks. You must use smaller weapons than Medium creatures. As a Small creature, you occupy a space of 5 feet by 5 feet. Your reach is 5 feet. (0)
Type You are a Humanoid with the derro subtype. (0)
Speed Your base speed is 20 feet. (–1)
Languages You begin play speaking Aklo and Undercommon. If you have a high Intelligence score, you can choose from any of the following languages: Abyssal, Common, Dwarven, Gnome, Goblin, and Terran. (0)
Alternate Species Traits
Darkvision You have darkvision 60 feet. (2)
Madness You are mentally disturbed, and suffer from certain peculiarities and obsessive behaviors. (Work with your GM to define these and how best to roleplay them.) You use your Charisma modifier on Will saves instead of your Wisdom modifier, and you are immune to confusion and insanity effects. You cannot be restored to sanity by any means short of a miracle or wish spell; if this occurs, you gain a +6 adjustment to Wisdom and a –6 adjustment to Charisma. (2)
Poison Use You are skilled in the use of poison and never risk accidentally poisoning yourself. (1)
Spell-Like Abilities 1/day—darkness, daze, and ghost sound. Your character level is your caster level, and Charisma is your casting ability. (3)
Spell Resistance You gain spell resistance equal to 6 + your character level. (2)
Vulnerable to Sunlight You take 1 point of Constitution damage after every hour you are exposed to sunlight. (–2)
Weapon Familiarity You are proficient with the aklys, chakram, light crossbow, and light repeating crossbow. You treat the crystal chakram Chr, fauchard AA2, and syringe spear AA as martial weapons instead of exotic weapons. (2)
Total: 11 RP (advanced)
Alternate Species Traits
Sunlight Acclimated Through special training and alchemical treatments, you were prepared by your people to spy on the surface world. You no longer take Constitution damage when exposed to sunlight, although sunlight is still painful to you. If exposed to sunlight for more than 1 continuous hour, your skin begins to blister and crack, and you suffer the sickened condition until you are no longer exposed to sunlight. This trait replaces the darkness spell-like ability and vulnerable to sunlight.
Feats
Improved Derro Spell-Like Abilities

Your arcane powers surge, giving you greater spell-like abilities.

Prerequisite(s): Cha 12, able to use derro spell-like abilities, derro, character level 3rd.

Benefit(s): You may use your ghost sound spell-like ability at will, and you add sound burst as a spell-like ability you can use once per day. Your caster level is equal to your character level, and Charisma is your casting ability.

Alternative Favored Class Bonuses
Alchemist Gain +1/6 of a new discovery.
Arcanist Add +1/4 to the number of times per day that you can use the consume spells class feature.
Barbarian Add a +1/2 bonus to your trap sense.
Bard Add a +1/2 bonus on Bluff checks to pass secret messages and a +1/2 bonus on Disguise checks to appear as a humanoid of the dwarf or gnome subtype.
Bloodrager Add +1/4 to your effective bloodrager class level when determining the strength of your bloodrager bloodline powers.
Fighter Choose the dirty trick or trip combat maneuver. Add +1/3 to your CMB when attempting this maneuver (maximum bonus of +4).
Investigator Add +1 extract formula from the investigator’s list to your formula book. This formula must be at least 1 level lower than the highest level of investigator formula you can create.
Magus Gain +1/6 of a new magus arcana.
Mesmerist Increase the number of mesmerist tricks you can use per day by +1/3.
Oracle Add +1/6 to your effective oracle level for the purpose of determining the effects of one revelation.
Psychic Gain +1/6 of a new phrenic amplification.
Rogue Add a +1/2 bonus on Stealth and Perception checks made while in dim light or darkness.
Slayer Add +1/2 on critical hit confirmation rolls for any attacks that deal nonlethal damage (maximum bonus of +4). This bonus does not stack with Critical Focus.
Sorcerer Select one bloodline power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Charisma modifier, or select the claws bloodline power of the abyssal bloodline. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that bloodline power, or +1 to the total number of rounds per day you can use the claws abyssal bloodline power.
Summoner Add +1 hit point to your eidolon.
Witch Gain +1/6 of a new witch hex.
Wizard Select one arcane school power at 1st level that is normally usable a number of times per day equal to 3 + your Intelligence modifier. Add +1/2 to the number of uses per day of that arcane school power.

Equipment

Crystal Chakram Chr

Shaped and carved from quartz or stranger subterranean crystals, these circular throwing discs have jagged razor-sharp edges. When a crystal chakram strikes a foe, the weapon shatters into tiny sharp fragments; if it misses, there is a 50% chance the chakram shatters when it hits the ground or another solid object; otherwise it can be retrieved and used again. A crystal chakram is treated as ammunition for the purpose of creating magic weapons.

Fighter Weapon Group: Thrown.

Fauchard

Like a glaive, the fauchard is a curved blade at the end of a pole. However, the cutting edge of a fauchard is along the concave side, like that of a sickle or scythe. The resulting weapon is more awkward to utilize (and as such is an exotic weapon), but its increased threat range over a glaive and the ability to trip foes make it a dangerous weapon in the hands of a skilled user.

Fighter Weapon Group: Polearms.

Syringe Spear

The blade of this weapon contains a thin tube or bore that connects to a hollow container just beneath the crosspiece. A successful hit with the spear injects the liquid contents of the container (typically poison) into the target. Refilling a syringe spear takes 1 minute. Fighter Weapon Group: Spears.

Additional Rules

For alchemist discoveries commonly used by derros (although not exclusive to them), see the Paizo campaign setting monster codex, page 23.
